content.text: Found it: `src/os.cc:243-267`, `long long file::size() const`. Let me quickly check the implementation to confirm the Windows high/low reconstruction logic.

**`src/os.cc`**, the method **`file::size()`** (spanning lines 243–267).

This is the function that, on Windows, calls `GetFileSize(handle, &size_upper)` to get the low 32 bits (return value) and high 32 bits (`size_upper` out-param), then reconstructs the 64-bit size via:

```cpp
unsigned long long long_size = size_upper;
return (long_size << sizeof(DWORD) * CHAR_BIT) | size_lower;
```

The POSIX branch of the same function (using `fstat`/`st_size`) is unaffected, matching the report that only Windows builds show truncated/garbage sizes for files >4GB — so the high/low combination logic in this Windows branch is exactly where to look.
